title: Shortest Block With All Different Letters

concept.title: Count the different letters inside the window
body: First find out how many different letters the whole word has: call it `total`. A block is "complete" when it contains all `total` different letters (each at least once). Keep a count per letter inside the window and a variable `distinct` that says how many letters have a positive count.

This is the same window pattern as the smallest window containing a given set of letters; here the "set" is simply all letters of the word, which is why the target does not have to be read from the input.

statement: A word contains some number of different letters. Find the length of its shortest block of consecutive letters that contains every one of those different letters at least once.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: Print the length of the shortest such block.

examples.note: The word has the letters a, b, c, d. The block dbca (length 4) contains all of them.

hints: Count how many different letters the whole word has.
Grow the window on the right until it contains all of them.
Then shrink it from the left while it still does, and record the shortest length.

explanation: The window grows until it has all the different letters of the word, then shrinks from the left as far as possible. The shortest length seen is the answer.

code.python:
s = input().strip()

total = len(set(s))
count = [0] * 26
distinct = 0
l = 0
best = len(s)
for rr, ch in enumerate(s):
    c = ord(ch) - ord("a")
    if count[c] == 0:
        distinct += 1
    count[c] += 1
    while distinct == total:
        best = min(best, rr - l + 1)
        d = ord(s[l]) - ord("a")
        count[d] -= 1
        if count[d] == 0:
            distinct -= 1
        l += 1
print(best)
